title: Lambdas & Method References
html:
A lambda is an anonymous function you can pass around as a value; a method reference is a lambda that just calls an existing method.

Lambda expression — (parameters) -> body — an instance of a functional interface, written inline. Introduced in Java 8, it replaced most anonymous inner classes.

Syntax forms

FormExample
No parameters() -> 42
One parameter (parentheses optional)s -> s.length()
Several parameters(a, b) -> a + b
Explicit types(String a, String b) -> a.compareTo(b)
var parameters (11+, allows annotations)(var a, var b) -> a + b
Block body (needs return)x -> { int y = x * 2; return y + 1; }

Capturing variables: effectively final

A lambda can read local variables from the enclosing method only if they are effectively final — never reassigned after initialisation. The lambda captures the value, and Java forbids the variable changing underneath it.

Fields are different

Fields (instance or static) are not restricted — a lambda reads them through this or the class. Only captured local variables must be effectively final.

this in a lambda vs an anonymous class

LambdaAnonymous class
this refers tothe enclosing instancethe anonymous object itself
New scope?No — can't redeclare an enclosing local nameYes — can shadow names
Implementsonly functional interfacesany interface or class, many methods, can hold state
Compiled toinvokedynamic + a private method (no extra .class file)a separate Outer$1.class

Method references — four kinds

When a lambda only forwards its arguments to one method, write Class::method instead.

KindSyntaxEquivalent lambda
Static methodInteger::parseInts -> Integer.parseInt(s)
Instance method of a particular objectSystem.out::printlnx -> System.out.println(x)
Instance method of an arbitrary object of a typeString::toUpperCases -> s.toUpperCase()
ConstructorArrayList::new() -> new ArrayList<>()
Watch out

System.out::println evaluates System.out once, when the reference is created — the lambda x -> System.out.println(x) looks it up on every call. Usually irrelevant, but a null receiver in obj::method throws NullPointerException immediately, not when called.

Are lambdas just syntactic sugar for anonymous classes?

No. They compile to an invokedynamic call site plus a private synthetic method; the JVM creates the implementation at run time (via LambdaMetafactory). No .class file per lambda, non-capturing lambdas are cached as singletons, and this means the enclosing instance rather than a new object.

Why must captured local variables be effectively final?

Locals live on the stack frame of the method, which may be gone by the time the lambda runs (e.g. on another thread). Java copies the value into the lambda; allowing later reassignment would make the copy silently stale and invite data races. Use a field, an array element or an AtomicInteger if you really need mutable state — or better, restructure with a stream reduction.

What does String::compareTo mean when a Comparator<String> is expected?

It's an unbound instance-method reference: the first parameter becomes the receiver. (a, b) -> a.compareTo(b). That's why a two-argument functional interface can be satisfied by a one-argument instance method.
